A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the late Cenozoicoic, the European mammal faunal record is well correlated with the magnetic time scale.

, in Europe, the late Gilbert magnetic subchron is represented by the Valles-Penedes and the Aragonian stages; the Gauss magnetic subchron by the Vallesian, Turolian and Ruscinian stages; and the lower Matuyama magnetic subchron by part of the Ruscinian stage, the MN 17–18 faunas and the early Villafranchian stage

, in the late Cenozoics of Europe, the Gauss magnetic chron is the time of the Triversa faunas, the Gilbert magnetic chron is the age of the Valensole faunal sequence, and the Matuyama magnetic chron is the period of the Hajnackae faunas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Valensole sequence is from the Gilbert, Gauss and Matuyama magnetic polarity chron sequence, in that order; the Triversa sequence is from the late Gilbert magnetic polarity chron; the Hajnackan sequence is from the Gauss magnetic polarity chron.
the magnetic polarity time scales of the last 3 million years are not only accurate but also very precise, with resolution on the order of 100,000 to 200,000 yr.
, in spite of the many problems of dating mammal faunas, there is now a good basis for correlating European late Cenosoic mammal faunal sequences with the magnetic polarity timescale.
